record.original_question: For each s, is the total sum h(s) of the sizes of all (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions equal to the explicit double-sum formula in Conjecture 11.3, and hence is the average size h(s)/f(s)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.3 The total sum h(s) of the sizes of all (s, s + 1, s + 2)-cores equals to h(s) = ... Equivalently, the average size of an (s, s + 1, s + 2)-core is h(s)/f(s).
Conjecture 11.1 through 11.4 have found resolutions and certain extensions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer s, an (s, s+1, s+2)-core partition is an integer partition λ none of whose hook lengths is equal to s, s+1, or s+2. The size |λ| of a partition is the sum of its parts. Let f(s) denote the number of (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions, and let h(s) denote the sum of |λ| over all (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions λ.

Prove or disprove the closed-form identity
$$h(s) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor s/2 \rfloor}\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor s/2\rfloor} \binom{s}{2k}\binom{s}{2j}\,C_k\,C_j\cdot W(k,j,s),$$
expressing h(s) as the explicit double sum (with Catalan numbers $C_k=\frac{1}{k+1}\binom{2k}{k}$ and an explicit weight $W(k,j,s)$ obtained from the standard generating-function derivation), and conclude that the average size of an (s, s+1, s+2)-core partition equals h(s)/f(s), where 
$$f(s) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor s/2\rfloor} \frac{1}{k+1}\binom{s}{2k}\binom{2k}{k}.$$

Equivalently, determine the total size and the average size of all (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions in closed form.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjectures on the number, largest size, and average size of (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions have been resolved. In particular, Amdeberhan and Leven (2014, arXiv:1406.2583) establish enumeration results for (s, s+1, s+2)-cores, and subsequent works (e.g., arXiv:1410.2061) confirm the largest- and average-size conjectures by analyzing the poset whose order ideals correspond to such cores.

status_evidence.claim: The enumeration of (s,s+1,s+2)-core partitions is settled.
